themes_detail.label: Food Safety Crisis Emerging
themes_detail.summary: Food poisoning complaints in Bed-Stuy spiked to 3 reports last week—a 500% increase over the 8-week baseline of 0.5 complaints per week—suggesting a potential foodborne illness cluster or restaurant hygiene breakdown that demands immediate investigation and health department coordination.
evidence: 3 food poisoning complaints filed last week vs. 0.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (500% spike, z-score 3.54)
Community Board has standing request to 'Increase health and safety inspections, e.g. for restaurants and childcare programs' with DOHMH
Spike is most recent and temporally concentrated (single week, not gradual)
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Department of Health to identify which restaurants/food vendors are under investigation; map the cluster geographically
Interview affected residents about symptoms, timeline, and which establishments they visited; determine if outbreak is linked to single source

themes_detail.label: Graffiti Surge Signals Disorder
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints jumped to 19 reports 3 weeks ago—a 182% spike over the 8-week baseline of 6.8 per week (z-score 3.75)—indicating either organized vandalism or deteriorating public space maintenance that warrants investigation into root causes and community safety implications.
evidence: 19 graffiti complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 6.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (182% increase, z-score 3.75, high severity)
Spike coincides with 'Obstruction' complaints also up 182% (12 vs. 4.2 avg) and 'Lot Condition' up 586% (6 vs. 0.9 avg)—suggests broader disorder pattern
Community Board historically requests park/amenity improvements and DPR funding, suggesting maintenance gaps
reporting_angles: Map the geographic distribution of graffiti complaints to identify hotspots; interview residents and business owners about visibility and fear of crime
Contact NYC Parks and NYPD to understand response times, cleanup capacity, and whether this reflects gang activity, youth groups, or systematic tagging campaign

themes_detail.label: Tree Damage & Requests Spike
themes_detail.summary: Tree-related complaints surged 3 weeks ago—'New Tree Request' up 1,100% (3 vs. 0.2 avg, z-score 6.35) and 'Illegal Tree Damage' up 414% (9 vs. 1.8 avg, z-score 4.64)—suggesting either environmental crisis, construction impact, or coordinated tree destruction warranting urgent investigation.
evidence: New Tree Request: 3 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.2 weekly average (1,100% increase, z-score 6.35, highest severity in dataset)
Illegal Tree Damage: 9 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 1.8 weekly average (414% increase, z-score 4.64, high severity)
854 DOB building permits filed in last 90 days (504 alterations, 147 new buildings, 98 ALT-CO projects) suggest construction activity may be damaging canopy
5 active ULURP rezonings in pipeline, including major projects (1166 Bedford, 862-868 Kent, Park Avenue rezoning)—potential tree removal for development
reporting_angles: Cross-reference DOB permits and ULURP applications with tree damage 311 complaints geographically; determine if construction/development is driving damage
Interview NYC Parks arborists about the surge; obtain records of illegal tree damage violations and developer citations
Assess impact on canopy coverage, air quality, and climate resilience; speak with environmental advocates and residents about losses

themes_detail.label: Lot Condition Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Lot condition complaints spiked to 6 reports 3 weeks ago—a 586% increase over the 8-week baseline of 0.9 per week (z-score 4.04)—indicating abandoned or poorly maintained vacant properties that may harbor illegal activity, blight, and public health hazards.
evidence: 6 lot condition complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.9 weekly average (586% spike, z-score 4.04, high severity)
Converges with graffiti (182% up), obstruction (182% up), and dumpster complaints (243% up)—suggests neighborhood-wide disorder/vacancy pattern
854 DOB permits with 147 new buildings and 98 ALT-CO projects may indicate properties mid-transition with inadequate interim maintenance
reporting_angles: Map vacant lots with 311 complaints; cross-reference ownership records to identify pattern of neglectful or speculative landlords
Interview neighbors about safety concerns (trespassing, dumping, rodent activity); contact NYC Department of Housing Preservation & Development about enforcement

themes_detail.label: Consumer Complaint Uptick
themes_detail.summary: Consumer complaints jumped to 10 reports 2 weeks ago—an 82% increase over the 8-week baseline of 5.5 per week (z-score 3.67)—potentially signaling a pattern of unfair business practices, fraud, or scams targeting Bed-Stuy residents that warrant pattern analysis.
evidence: 10 consumer complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 5.5 weekly average (82% increase, z-score 3.67, high severity)
Timing and spike suggest recent trigger; nature of complaints requires deeper investigation
reporting_angles: Request detailed complaint data from NYC Department of Consumer Affairs; identify common categories (landlord/tenant, retail fraud, utilities, financial services, etc.)
Interview affected consumers about complaint types and whether a single business or scam is driving the spike
